result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend one bundled, subsetted font, give the offline and prepaid-data reasons, ask about scripts, and call for tabular figures. B wins because it gives a real fallback stack that ends in system-ui and sans-serif. A gives no stack and simply assumes Roboto is on every device. A does better on reaching 'friendly' through spacing, color and corner radii, and on suggesting system text for dense content. B also adds checks for the currency symbol and font-synthesis. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend one bundled, subsetted font and tie that to offline use and prepaid data. Both also flag tabular figures and the need to check script coverage. B does a bit better because it gives a rough payload size, suggests system text for dense content, and says friendliness can come from spacing, radii and colour rather than the typeface. B also names Noto for non-Latin scripts. A is the only one to give an explicit stack ending in a generic family, though both assume Roboto is on every Android device.
